title: Intel mature DCAI margin adjudication after the richer-mix forecast
chronology: Selected before viewing any new equity output or reverse margin hurdle. No equity calculation, source-model mutation or valuation-based tuning in this task. Earlier published/researched operating outcomes are known.

owned_judgment.range_meaning: An owned business-outcome range, not an estimated confidence interval or prescribed valuation grid.32% remains a defensible cautious case; it is not established as the most likely mature margin by the available evidence.
owned_judgment.reason: The current internal-transfer model has already produced DCAI margins above40%. Richer CPU mix and demand provide operating leverage, while the model continues substantial node R&D/manufacturing costs in Foundry and corporate SBC separately. Competition and a larger custom-silicon mix justify some normalization, but32% embeds considerably more CPU margin erosion than mix dilution alone.35% balances persistent CPU IP/value and scale against procurement bargaining and custom mix.
owned_judgment.why_not40central: Q3 is a scarcity/ramp quarter, not a normalized cycle. Competitive2025 ASP reductions, customer concentration, AMD/Arm alternatives and continued costly product transitions prevent treating40%+ as protected. Lower-margin purpose-built silicon grows faster, and its mature segment profit is undisclosed.
owned_judgment.why_not32central: With mature Other DCAI near one-quarter of sales,32% implies CPU operating margin about36% if Other earns20%.35% instead implies roughly40% CPU margin. Neither is observed segment disaggregation, but the latter is more consistent with a durable high-value CPU franchise after market-like fabrication charges, without assuming the current blended42% persists.
owned_judgment.group_boundary: 35% is the DCAI segment margin, not consolidated group cash margin. Preserve Foundry manufacturing/process-R&D costs, corporate cash-equivalent SBC/overhead, leases/NCI and other existing costs once. Do not add the same process improvement to both DCAI and Foundry. No new consolidated-margin target is asserted.
owned_judgment.cost_basis: Existing physical output, host capital/D&A/WC and packaging investment remain unchanged. The revised margin is a different retained-product-economics forecast on the same accepted sales, not additional free capacity or a separate yield-reduction credit.

implementation_if_adopted.post2030: For each year2031–2040, add0.003*(year-2030) to the original aggregate DCAI margin; from2040 onward add0.03. This is equivalent to moving both the paired underlying DCAI terminal margin and the incremental ASP-retention terminal margin from32% to35%, retaining their prior linear fade timing. Products EBIT increases by the margin addition times DCAI sales; all other operating fields remain unchanged.
implementation_if_adopted.no_changes: No revenue, unit, ASP, physical capital, D&A, WC, Foundry dollar profit, separate packaging, corporate, tax, financing or claim policy changes. There is no tax or equity calculation in this addendum.

primary_evidence.locator: Recast MD&A pages2–4, segment accounting and annual segment table
primary_evidence.facts: Recast2021–2023 applies internal foundry market-like transfer charges and separates Altera. DCAI2021 revenue20.786B/operating profit9.071B;2022 revenue16.856B/profit4.198B;2023 revenue12.635B/profit1.620B. These correspond to43.64%,24.91%,12.82%. They establish possible cyclicality under the transfer model, not a directly invariant current DCAI series; subsequent NEX/other reallocations changed scope.

primary_evidence.locator: Intel Products MD&A table and Note3 Operating Segments
primary_evidence.facts: Latest annual recast DCAI revenue/profit:B2023 15.980/.945;2024 16.125/1.414;2025 16.919/3.422, or5.91%/8.77%/20.23%. Products margins23%/26%/26% rounded.2025 DCAI improvement included1.5B lower operating expenses and lower Gaudi inventory charges; higher server unit costs largely offset higher revenue. Intersegment charges aim to approximate market prices; manufacturing/process-development/excess-capacity costs reside in Foundry. Corporate SBC is not in segment margins.

primary_evidence.locator: Note3 segment tables; Intel Products MD&A
primary_evidence.facts: H1 DCAI revenue11.314B/profit4.016B;Q2 revenue6.262B/profit2.474B. Therefore Q1 by subtraction5.052B/1.542B. Margins30.52%Q1,39.51%Q2,35.50%H1. Revenue/ramp leverage is already visible; no assumption that every subsequent quarter compounds this improvement.

Q3 DCAI revenue7.318B/profit3.039B=41.53%. Reported product profit rose2.2B despite higher premium unit costs;segment profit rose2.1B. Premium mix dominates ASP gains and input-cost pricing contributes less. Corporate unallocated includes SBC. These observations support operating leverage, but not a measured long-run CPU/custom margin split.

primary_evidence.locator: CFO segment discussion and Q4 gross-margin discussion
primary_evidence.facts: Granite Rapids became largest server family; DCAI demand still exceeded supply. Purpose-built silicon grew above50% sequentially and above100%YoY;its strong expected Q4 growth makes gross-margin comparisons more difficult. This is evidence for mix pressure, not an explicit20% operating-margin disclosure.

Historical management aspiration was60% Products non-GAAP gross margin/40% operating margin by2030, with market-priced manufacturing charges. This was a prior leadership target, not current confirmed guidance or the basis for adopting35%. Its scope differs from DCAI and excludes adjustments.

primary_evidence.locator: Server CPU supply and competitive-share forecast
primary_evidence.facts: Independent primary market-research forecast supports strong market growth but constrained Intel supply and growing competitors. It informs competitive risk, not a future profit-margin measurement.

mix_diagnostic.source: Frozen ASP policy annual operating rows, not observed future mix
mix_diagnostic.formula: DCAI margin=(1-other_share)*CPU margin+other_share*Other margin. Illustrative Other margin is not publicly disclosed and includes more than a single custom-silicon product.
mix_diagnostic.interpretation: A rise in Other sales share alone does not explain the full42-to32point decline; lower CPU profitability must also be assumed.35% still allows meaningful erosion and custom mix dilution. Neither blend should be represented as source-calibrated to a precise mature margin.

falsifiers.lower_view: Sustained ASP gains fail to translate into absolute product profit after cost pass-through, premium-chip costs stay elevated as volume scales, or custom revenue rises while CPU pricing/renewal economics deteriorate. Those would favor30–32%.
falsifiers.higher_view: CPU gross profit grows with accepted output after supply shortages ease, custom margins improve with scale, and incremental product spending remains disciplined without shifting unrecognized costs into Foundry/corporate. Those would favor high30s/40%.
falsifiers.strongest_objection: The scale and mix in2040 are far beyond current observations. Powerful hyperscalers and architectural alternatives may capture much of the value;35% is still a business judgment, not demonstrated durable market power.
falsifiers.competition_use: A3–5-year pitch should rely on observable2027–2029 product-profit conversion and paid capacity delivery. A terminal margin choice alone is not a defensible directional catalyst.
